title: The reference says what a domain is
statement: The domain table's description in the schema, shown in the reference, MUST say that a domain is for one business capability, and the `domain-named-for-technology` check's explanation MUST say that a domain is a vertical slice of business capability whose technology is written as the technical records that implement its design.

title: The modeling skill finds the capabilities first
statement: The plugin's modeling skill MUST start, before any record is written, by finding the product's business capabilities and making each one a domain, and MUST list the questions that tell a capability from a technology layer.

title: Each domain says its subdomain type
statement: Each domain MUST say its subdomain type: core for the product's edge, supporting or generic, which guides how much modeling it deserves.

title: Every use case sits under a capability with a whole-number position
statement: A capability MUST sit under a domain and give its place in a required `position`. Every use case MUST sit under one of its domain's capabilities.

title: A use case under a capability belongs to the capability's domain
statement: A use case, and everything under it, MUST belong to the capability's domain, so that its obligations count in that domain's coverage exactly as they did directly under the domain.

title: A repository persists one aggregate
statement: A repository MUST persist exactly one aggregate, and an aggregate MUST have exactly one repository. Code that keeps several aggregates splits into one repository each; an aggregate no repository persists is an `aggregate-without-repository` gap.

title: Domain services and terms are in the schema
statement: The schema MUST have `domain_service` under a domain, which its commands and queries `calls`, and `term` under a domain for its glossary.

title: A schema change takes effect on the next load
statement: A changed migration MUST take effect on the next load with no other code change: the store applies the migrations in order, records them, and reads the schema back from the database. The database is rebuilt from the data files, so there are no upgrade migrations.

title: Existing data is checked against the changed schema
statement: After a schema change, every product's data MUST be loaded against the new schema, so that a change which breaks existing data shows as `data-refused` errors straight away, and a change that would leave rows without a table is refused.

title: The row types and the reference follow the schema
statement: The row types in `lathe/src/platform/data/tables.ts` and the committed reference MUST be generated from the schema, and a test MUST fail when either differs from what the schema gives.

title: Kinds and relations are the schema, not code
statement: Every kind and every relation MUST be a table of the schema with its meta_kind or meta_relation rows, defined by the numbered migrations in `lathe/schema/` or generated from a product's declarations. The engine, the checks and the app MUST NOT hard-code the list of kinds or relations.

title: Lathe's schema changes only by a migration
statement: Lathe's own kinds, columns and relations MUST change only by a new numbered migration in `lathe/schema/`, reviewed in git. The app, the API and the aggregates' commands MUST NOT change the schema: no command writes a meta table.

title: Obligations and link roles come only from the schema
statement: Which kinds are obligations MUST come only from each kind's `obligation` flag in the schema, and a product's own obligation kinds MUST be designed and proved only by links of relations whose role is design or proof.

title: Every table, column, kind and relation of Lathe's is described
statement: Lathe's tables, columns, kinds and relations MUST each have a description, as comments in its migrations, and every check row its summary and explanation.

title: A breaking schema change raises the schema version and brings a converter
statement: Lathe's schema version MUST be one whole number, kept only in `lathe/schema/version.json` and starting at 1. A schema change that existing data may not pass (a renamed or removed table or column, a new required column, a narrower rule) MUST raise it by one, MUST add the converter `lathe/upgrades/<from>-to-<to>.ts` that moves the data forward exactly one version, and MUST raise the package's major version; a change every existing product still passes MUST NOT.

title: Each test sits under what it tests, as that thing's test kind
statement: Each test MUST be of the test kind named after what it tests or its owner, and sit under that one record, the only obligation it proves.

title: A product kind gets a table of its own
statement: A product_kind row MUST give the product a table named after the kind, with an ID, a title, a required column for its parent kind and a column for each of its fields, typed and required as declared; an obligation kind MUST join the obligation supertype.

title: A product kind keeps its own label, stage and obligation
statement: A product kind MUST be listed after Lathe's kinds, with its own label, stage and obligation, in any of the six stages or none, and MUST NOT change any of Lathe's kinds.

title: A product relation adds a link table or a pair
statement: A product_relation with a new name MUST get a link table of its own; one with Lathe's name MUST add only its pair, and MUST change nothing else of that relation.

title: A kind declared twice is refused, naming its file and line
statement: Two product_kind rows with the same name MUST be refused by the store, naming the file and line of the second and the line of the first.

title: A product relation declared twice is refused, naming the file and line
statement: The store MUST refuse a `product_relation` row with the same name, source kind and target kind as another, once, naming its file and line.

title: A pattern sits under the product and use cases or domains follow it
statement: A pattern MUST sit under a product and MAY list its settings as pattern_setting rows. A use case, or a domain, MAY follow one or more patterns with the `follows` relation.

title: A pattern rule is owed by every domain that follows it, and proved per domain
statement: A pattern rule MUST be an obligation of each domain that follows its pattern, or has a use case that does, proved by one pattern rule test per rule and domain.

title: A use case has a flow per interface, whose steps reach operations and views
statement: The schema MUST have an `interface` under each product, of kind web app, API, CLI, agent tools, desktop or other, and at most one `flow` per use case and interface, naming its interface, with `flow_step` under it with a required `position` and `path`; a step MAY fulfill its use case's requirements, invoke a command or query, happen in a view and exchange with integrations.

title: A requirement a flow misses is a gap
statement: A UC requirement that no step of one of its use case's flows fulfills MUST be reported as not designed, naming the flows that miss it.

title: A flow's ID ends in its interface's number
statement: A flow's ID MUST be its use case's ID, FL and its interface's number (TL-LEND-UC01-FL01 goes through TL-IF01), and its interface MUST be of its own product; `next-id` MUST give a use case's next flow through the first interface it has no flow through.

title: Steps fit their interface
statement: A step of a flow through an API, a CLI or agent tools MUST NOT happen in a view, and a step of an API flow that invokes a command or query no endpoint exposes MUST be warned of (step-without-endpoint).

title: A flow test runs at its interface's level
statement: A flow test SHOULD run at browser for a web app or desktop flow and at system for an API, CLI or agent tools flow, manual or automated alike; one at another level MUST be warned of (flow-test-level-for-interface).

title: An interface no flow goes through is a gap
statement: An interface no flow goes through MUST be reported as a gap (interface-without-flow).

title: Each use case command changes one use case, held to its rules
statement: Each command of the Use case aggregate MUST load the use case it changes whole through its repository, hold it to the aggregate's rules before it saves, and write only the aggregate's own tables; a refused command MUST give every reason and change no file.

title: A record of a use case goes with what it holds, refused while referenced
statement: Removing a use case, or a requirement, flow, step or test in one, MUST take what sits under it and the links they start, and MUST be refused, naming what does, while anything left still references them.

title: Every interface names the use case command it runs
statement: The CLI (lathe use-case <command>), the MCP tools (one per command and query) and HTTP (POST /api/use-case/<command>) MUST each name the one command they run, each taking the command's own fields, checked against the schema's columns.

title: A use case with no flow is a coverage gap, never an error
statement: A use case with no flow MUST be reported in its domain's coverage as a `use-case-without-flow` gap, a record short of a minimum. It MUST NOT be an error, so `lathe check` does not fail because of it.

title: Requirements and rules may name a group
statement: A `uc_requirement`, `view_requirement`, `api_requirement`, `pattern_rule` or `standard_rule` MAY name a short heading in `group_name`, such as Validation or Paging, so that a long list of them is sorted under headings as a real product sorts it. A group is a column, not a record, so renaming one MUST change no ID.

title: A path whose positions skip a number is a step-order error
statement: The steps on each path of a flow SHOULD run 1, 2, 3 without a gap, the path compared trimmed and in any letter case. A path whose positions skip a number MUST be reported once as a `step-order` error, on the first step after the gap.

title: The engine loads the stages and each kind's stage and position
statement: The engine MUST load the stages in order and each kind's stage and position from the schema. The product and open questions MUST sit outside the stages.

title: A product places its own kinds in a stage
statement: A product kind MAY name one of the six stages, or none, and MUST NOT add a stage or change one of Lathe's kinds.

title: Kinds are read in one order, the schema's
statement: Every list of kinds, in the app, the reference and coverage, MUST read them in one order: Lathe's kinds by their position in the schema (the product, then stage by stage, each kind by its position, then open questions), then a product's own kinds by name. No code MAY keep a list of its own.

title: Entities, their fields and invariants are in the schema
statement: The schema MUST have `entity` under an aggregate requiring `role`, its `entity_field` rows, `has_one` and `has_many` from entity to entity, and `invariant` under an aggregate with a required statement. The reference MUST describe them.

title: An entity's fields are its entity_field rows
statement: The engine MUST give each entity its entity_field rows as its fields, in position order, each with a name, a meaning, exactly one type, whether it is required, and a column name and example when they help. An entity, event or read model with no fields MUST be reported as a gap.

title: Another aggregate is referenced by ID, through a field
statement: A reference to another aggregate MUST be a field typed by that aggregate. In its own domain its table MAY hold a foreign key; a foreign key MUST NOT point into another domain, where the reference stays a plain ID.

title: Uniqueness is an invariant its rule enforces
statement: A rule that no two records share a value MUST be an invariant, enforced by its rule; a unique key that backs it up in the database MUST name it.

title: Each Aggregate command changes one aggregate, held to its rules
statement: Each command of the Aggregate aggregate (LA-AUT-A6) MUST load the aggregate it changes whole through AggregateRepository, hold it to the aggregate's rules before it saves and write only the aggregate's own tables; a refused command MUST give every reason and change no file. The CLI (lathe aggregate <command>), the aggregate_ MCP tools and HTTP (POST /api/aggregate/<command>) MUST each name the one command they run.

title: A child entity its root does not reach is an entity-unreferenced warning
statement: Each child entity SHOULD be reached from its aggregate's root by `has_one` or `has_many` links inside the aggregate. One that is not MUST be reported as an `entity-unreferenced` warning naming it and its root; an aggregate without exactly one root MUST NOT have its children judged.

title: The reference script prints the reference, or writes it to a file
statement: The reference script (`npm --prefix lathe run reference`) MUST write the reference as Markdown: how data is kept, then the kinds with their tables, the other tables, the relations, the stages and the checks, each with its own anchor. With `--print` it MUST print it, and with `--out <file>` write it to that file.

title: The reference gives every fact of each kind, table, relation, stage and check
statement: The reference MUST give each kind's label, description, stage, parents and children, obligation (yes or no), ID pattern and ID scope; each table's role, keys and columns with their types, values, references and descriptions; each relation's role, labels, description and pairs; each stage's position, label and description; and each check's name, severity, summary, explanation and kinds. The engine's own problem, `data-refused`, MUST be listed as a check too, and the reference MUST say that clean architecture's use case is a command handler in Lathe.

title: A product's reference shows its own kinds and its own checks
statement: The reference MUST be the product's own: its kinds, tables and relations with its declarations, and its own checks after Lathe's and the engine's.

title: Lathe's committed reference never goes stale
statement: Lathe's reference MUST be committed as `lathe/REFERENCE.md`, so an agent can read it without running anything. The package build MUST regenerate it, and a test MUST fail when the committed file differs from what the reference script writes. It is generated from the schema and the check rows, never written by hand.

title: What the reference would leave blank is refused
statement: The store MUST refuse a product kind or relation without a description, and a check row without its summary or explanation; Lathe's own tables, kinds and checks MUST all be described.

title: Relations read in plain words from both ends
statement: Each relation MUST carry a `forward_label`, the link read from its source ("Raises"), and a `reverse_label`, the link read from its target ("Raised by"), in sentence case. The reference MUST show both and list each kind's links out by their forward labels and its links in by their reverse labels. The store MUST refuse a product relation without both.

title: Commands and policies are in the schema
statement: The schema MUST have `command` under the entity it changes with `raises` and `checks`, and `policy` under the command it invokes with `hears`. The reference MUST describe them.

title: A command changes only its own aggregate
statement: A command MUST change exactly its own aggregate: the one the entity it sits under belongs to, and no other. Where a change seems to reach another aggregate, the model changes: the other aggregate reacts to an event through a policy, or the two are one aggregate.

title: Each Command command changes one command, held to its rules
statement: Each command of the Command aggregate (LA-AUT-A8) MUST load the command it changes whole through CommandRepository, hold it to the aggregate's rules before it saves and write only the aggregate's own tables; a refused command MUST give every reason and change no file. The CLI (lathe command <command>), the command_ MCP tools and HTTP (POST /api/command/<command>) MUST each name the one command they run.

title: Tests start from test data sets
statement: A test data set MUST sit under a domain and MAY give the environment, accounts and starting records some tests need, how to prepare and reset them, and the seed or fixture file that builds them; any kind of test MAY start from any number of them, each a starts_from link.

title: A data set nothing uses, or whose file is missing, is reported
statement: A test data set no test starts from MUST be reported as an error, and one whose file does not exist MUST be reported: as an error when an automated test starts from it, else as a warning.

title: A kind or check met while reading opens its page in one step
statement: Wherever the Reader meets a kind or a check while reading the spec (a record's kind, a problem's code, a column), they MUST be able to open what the reference says about it in one step, without leaving the workbench.

title: Standards, their tests and meets are in the schema
statement:
The schema MUST have a `standard` kind under the product and a `standard_rule` kind under a standard, in the technical specification stage, with IDs `

-STD-` and `-R`; a `standard_rule_test` kind under a standard rule, in the test plan stage, with IDs `-T`, any number per rule, at any level; and the relation `meets` from a technical record to a standard rule, labeled Meets and Met by, with no role. The reference MUST describe them.

title: A standard rule is owed, met by technical records and proved by its tests
statement: A standard rule MUST be an obligation of the product: designed and built by the technical records that meet it, and proved by its standard rule tests, automated or manual, whose file names them. One that nothing meets MUST be reported as not designed, and one with no such test as not proved.

title: Each technical record sits under the record it builds and names its file
statement: Each technical record MUST sit under the record it builds, as its kind says: a data model and a table under an entity, a read model or its domain; a projection under a read model; a command handler under a command; a query handler under a query; an event handler under a policy; an event type under an event; a value type under a value object; a predicate under a specification; an endpoint handler under an endpoint; an adapter under an integration; a repository, a service and a UI component under their domain. It MAY name its file, relative to the repo root; a file that does not exist yet is work still to do.

title: A table stores only what fields can't say
statement: A table's columns MUST follow from its entity's or read model's fields, with value objects flattened; the table MUST store its name, its storage and its keys, and a unique key MAY name the invariant it enforces.

title: A record can point at the code that builds or proves it
statement: A technical record MUST be able to name its `file`, and a test its run by's `file` that runs it, each as a path relative to the repo root.

title: Each Table command changes one table, held to its rules
statement: Each command of the Table aggregate (LA-AUT-A18) MUST load the table it changes whole through TableRepository, hold it to the aggregate's rules before it saves and write only the aggregate's own tables; a refused command MUST give every reason and change no file. The CLI (lathe table <command>), the table_ MCP tools and HTTP (POST /api/table/<command>) MUST each name the one command they run.

title: A view exists because steps happen in it
statement: A view MUST have no owner, its product following from its ID, and one that no step happens in MUST be reported as an error.

title: A view rule is a view requirement
statement: A rule of a view MUST be a view requirement under its view, proved by its view tests.

title: Each View command changes one view
statement: Each command of the View aggregate (LA-AUT-A12) MUST load the view it changes whole through ViewRepository and write only the aggregate's own tables; a refused command MUST give every reason and change no file. The CLI (lathe view <command>), the view_ MCP tools and HTTP (POST /api/view/<command>) MUST each name the one command they run.

title: Both sides' rows are kept, sorted
statement: The merge driver MUST keep the rows each side added, and a change or a removal made on one side only, keep one copy of a row both sides added alike, and write the merged file sorted by key.

title: A real clash fails the merge, naming it
statement: The merge driver MUST fail, exiting 1 and naming the clash, when one key is added on both sides with different content, or one row is changed on both sides or removed on one and changed on the other.

title: The merged table's own rules are checked
statement: The merge driver MUST check the merged file against its table's own rules (columns, types, keys and checks) and fail on a row that breaks them; keys to other tables MUST be checked when the data next loads.

title: Git runs the driver for every data file
statement: The merge driver MUST run as `lathe merge-data %O %A %B %P` for every file `.gitattributes` names with `merge=lathe-data`, writing the merge over ours as git expects.

title: Specifications are in the schema
statement: The schema MUST have `specification` with no owner, reading one or more aggregates of one domain with `reads`, which commands `checks` and queries `selects_by`, with a required statement.

title: A specification nothing uses is an error
statement: A specification that no command checks and no query selects by MUST be reported as an error naming it, whose message says to use it or remove it.

title: Each Specification command changes one specification
statement: Each command of the Specification aggregate (LA-AUT-A5) MUST load the specification it changes whole through SpecificationRepository and write only the aggregate's own tables; a refused command MUST give every reason and change no file. The CLI (lathe specification <command>), the specification_ MCP tools and HTTP (POST /api/specification/<command>) MUST each name the one command they run.

title: Read models and queries are in the schema
statement: The schema MUST have `read_model` under a domain with its fields and `reads`, and `query` under the one read model it reads.

title: Each Read model command changes one read model, held to its rules
statement: Each command of the Read model aggregate (LA-AUT-A10) MUST load the read model it changes whole through ReadModelRepository, hold it to the aggregate's rules before it saves and write only the aggregate's own tables; a refused command MUST give every reason and change no file. The CLI (lathe read-model <command>), the read_model_ MCP tools and HTTP (POST /api/read-model/<command>) MUST each name the one command they run.

title: A business outcome sits under its product and is measurable
statement: A business outcome MUST sit under its product and give a statement of the outcome, its measure and its target; the store MUST refuse one that leaves any of them out.

title: Capabilities serve outcomes, many to many
statement: A capability MAY serve any number of its product's business outcomes, and an outcome MAY be served by any number of capabilities, each a serves link from the capability; only a capability serves, and only an outcome is served.

title: Discovery is the first stage
statement: Discovery MUST be the first stage, before the domain model, and hold the business outcomes, which follow the product in the kinds' order.

title: Tests and the product's own records measure outcomes
statement: A business outcome MAY be measured by any number of tests of any kind, each a measured_by link from the outcome, and a test MAY measure several outcomes. A record of a product's own kind (a report, a script, a check row) MAY measure one only once the product allows that kind with a product_relation named measured_by; no other kind of Lathe's measures. An outcome that nothing in the code can measure MAY say instead how it is measured outside the code.

title: A product names its roles and interfaces
statement: A product MUST list the roles its use cases name as actors and the interfaces its flows go through, each interface of one kind: web app, desktop, API, CLI, agent tools or other.

title: An open question sits where it is asked
statement: An open question MUST sit under its product or one of its domains and MAY be about any records of its product; a decided question is removed with its links, its answer written into the records it affects.

title: Value objects and their constraints are in the schema
statement: The schema MUST have `value_object` with no owner, its `value_object_field` rows, and `constraint` under it with a required statement. The reference MUST describe them.

title: A value object nothing uses is an error
statement: A value object that no entity, event or read model field is typed by MUST be reported as an error naming it, whose message says to use it or remove it.

title: Each Value object command changes one value object
statement: Each command of the Value object aggregate (LA-AUT-A9) MUST load the value object it changes whole through ValueObjectRepository and write only the aggregate's own tables; a refused command MUST give every reason and change no file. The CLI (lathe value-object <command>), the value_object_ MCP tools and HTTP (POST /api/value-object/<command>) MUST each name the one command they run.

title: Domain events are in the schema
statement: The schema MUST have `domain_event` under an aggregate with `published`, its `event_field` rows and its `event_type`. The reference MUST describe them.

title: An event's fields are its event_field rows, as an entity's
statement: The engine MUST give each domain event its event_field rows as its fields. An event with no fields MUST be reported as a gap, and the store MUST refuse a field without a name, or named twice.

title: An event a policy hears is delivered by outbox
statement: An event a policy hears, whose aggregate is stored in a table, and whose event type does not give `outbox` as its delivery MUST be reported as an `event-not-by-outbox` warning naming the event and its policies. An event that only keeps read models current (fed_by), where those read models are rebuilt from the data on every load, MAY be delivered in process, and MUST NOT be reported, whether it is published or not.

title: Each Domain event command changes one domain event
statement: Each command of the Domain event aggregate (LA-AUT-A7) MUST load the domain event it changes whole through DomainEventRepository and write only the aggregate's own tables; a refused command MUST give every reason and change no file. The CLI (lathe domain-event <command>), the domain_event_ MCP tools and HTTP (POST /api/domain-event/<command>) MUST each name the one command they run.

title: An endpoint exposes one command or query
statement: An endpoint MUST sit under the one command or query it exposes, and a flow step MUST reach it through that command or query, never directly.

title: An endpoint rule is an API requirement
statement: A rule of an endpoint MUST be an API requirement under its endpoint, proved by its endpoint tests.

title: Each Endpoint command changes one endpoint
statement: Each command of the Endpoint aggregate (LA-AUT-A13) MUST load the endpoint it changes whole through EndpointRepository and write only the aggregate's own tables; a refused command MUST give every reason and change no file. The CLI (lathe endpoint <command>), the endpoint_ MCP tools and HTTP (POST /api/endpoint/<command>) MUST each name the one command they run.

title: An integration exists because steps exchange with it
statement: An integration MUST have no owner, its product following from its ID, and one that no step exchanges with MUST be reported as an error.

title: Each Integration command changes one integration
statement: Each command of the Integration aggregate (LA-AUT-A14) MUST load the integration it changes whole through IntegrationRepository and write only the aggregate's own tables; a refused command MUST give every reason and change no file. The CLI (lathe integration <command>), the integration_ MCP tools and HTTP (POST /api/integration/<command>) MUST each name the one command they run.

title: A UI component renders views, and one that renders none is an error
statement: A UI component MUST sit under its domain, name its file, link each view it renders with `renders` and each view requirement its code does with `builds`; one that renders no view MUST be reported as an error naming it, whose message says to use it or remove it.

title: Each UI component command changes one UI component
statement: Each command of the UI component aggregate (LA-AUT-A15) MUST load the UI component it changes whole through UiComponentRepository and write only the aggregate's own tables; a refused command MUST give every reason and change no file. The CLI (lathe ui-component <command>), the ui_component_ MCP tools and HTTP (POST /api/ui-component/<command>) MUST each name the one command they run.

title: An entry point names the file that starts it
statement: An entry point MUST sit under its domain, be titled by its identifier exactly as in code, and name the file that starts the product or one of its processes.

title: Tooling names its script or configuration
statement: A tooling record MUST sit under its domain, be titled by its identifier exactly as in code, and name the script or configuration file that builds, checks or tests the product.

title: Storage requirements are obligations under an aggregate or read model
statement: The schema MUST have `storage_requirement`, an obligation under exactly one aggregate or read model with a required statement, and `storage_requirement_test` under it; coverage MUST count it designed by construction, built only when its aggregate's repository or its read model's reader names a file that exists and its data store, and proved by one of its tests.

title: Each Storage requirement command changes one storage requirement
statement: Each command of the Storage requirement aggregate (LA-AUT-A22) MUST load the storage requirement it changes whole through StorageRequirementRepository and write only the aggregate's own tables; a refused command MUST give every reason and change no file. The CLI (lathe storage-requirement <command>), the storage_requirement_ MCP tools and HTTP (POST /api/storage-requirement/<command>) MUST each name the one command they run.

title: Every repository, reader and table names its one data store
statement: The schema MUST have `data_store`, under a product or one of its domains, with its kind, and the relations `stored_in` (each repository, reader or table to at most one data store) and `provided_by` (a data store to at most one integration); coverage MUST report a repository, reader or table that names no data store, and a data store nothing is kept in.

title: Each Data store command changes one data store
statement: Each command of the Data store aggregate (LA-AUT-A23) MUST load the data store it changes whole through DataStoreRepository and write only the aggregate's own tables; a refused command MUST give every reason and change no file. The CLI (lathe data-store <command>), the data_store_ MCP tools and HTTP (POST /api/data-store/<command>) MUST each name the one command they run.

title: The check prints errors, then warnings, then coverage
statement: `lathe check` MUST print every error, then every warning, then one coverage line per domain and obligation kind, each showing how many are designed, built and proved out of the total." (was "for requirements and for domain rules

title: The check exits non-zero on any error
statement: `lathe check` MUST exit with status 1 when there is at least one error, and with status 0 otherwise. Warnings MUST NOT change the exit status.

title: The check can print each product's whole workspace as JSON
statement: With `--json`, `lathe check` MUST print, instead of the text report, `{ products: [{ root, workspace }] }`: each product the workspace shows, its folder from the workspace root and its whole `Workspace`.

title: Data that breaks the schema is refused, and is an error
statement: The store MUST refuse each row that breaks the schema (a duplicate or malformed ID, an unknown column, a missing title, parent or required column, a parent or link naming a record that does not exist or of a kind it does not allow, a link into another product), and `lathe check` MUST report each refusal as a `data-refused` error naming the file, the line and the rule. An automated test whose file is missing, or does not name the test's ID, MUST be an error naming the test." (was "does not name what it proves

title: A data file that does not load is an error, not a crash
statement: A data file that cannot be loaded (a line that is not JSON, a value of the wrong type, a row the schema refuses) MUST become `data-refused` errors naming the file, the line and the rule, and `lathe check` MUST report them without crashing. Nothing else MAY be checked until the data loads.

title: Every problem names its check and its record
statement: Every problem MUST name the check that found it and, when it concerns a record, that record's ID, and its message MUST be a plain sentence naming the IDs involved.

title: A test runs at a level its kind allows
statement: A test whose run by level its kind does not allow MUST be reported as a `test-level-not-allowed` warning naming the test, its level and the levels its kind allows (LA-TRC-DS02), and MUST count as proof of nothing (LA-TRC-UC02-R07).

title: A new check needs only a new check row
statement: Adding a check MUST need only a new check row, added with the Check aggregate's Add a check command (`lathe check add-check`). It MUST NOT need a change to the engine's TypeScript.

title: Checks can read every typed table
statement: A check's query MUST be able to read every typed table, the `record_parent`, `link` and `record_group` views, the `record_scope` table, the `meta_*` tables, the coverage tables and the product's settings, each a typed column of `product_setting` with its default when the product has no row. The file facts (`file_facts`: whether a test's or a technical record's file exists, and whether a test's file names the test's ID) MUST be filled before the checks run, so checks stay in SQL.

title: Every check runs, in order, even after one fails
statement: The engine MUST run every check row on every load, in the order of LA-CHK-DS01, and MUST collect the problems of all of them in that order, even when one check fails to run.

title: Each Check command changes one check
statement: Each command of the Check aggregate (LA-CHK-A1) MUST load the check it changes whole through CheckRepository and write only the aggregate's own tables; a refused command MUST give every reason and change no file. The CLI (lathe check <command>), the check_ MCP tools and HTTP (POST /api/check/<command>) MUST each name the one command they run.

title: A product's check rows run after Lathe's checks
statement: The engine MUST run every check row with the product's `product_id` after all of Lathe's checks, in `position` order, against the same tables, and MUST read the same `record`, `message` and `severity` columns from each. A product with no check rows of its own MUST run only Lathe's checks, and a product's check MUST report only on records of its product.

title: A product check's name comes from its row
statement: A product check's problems MUST be named by its row's `name`, as Lathe's checks are, whatever its query returns in a column of its own.

title: A product check named like one of Lathe's checks is refused
statement: The store MUST refuse a product check row whose name one of Lathe's checks has, naming `lathe/data/check.jsonl`, so the row never runs; the same row written into a data file MUST be a `data-refused` error.

title: A product check that fails to run is an error naming the check
statement: A product check whose query fails to run MUST be reported as an error under its check name, saying that the check could not run and why, and the other checks MUST still run.

title: lathe.config.json refuses a checks setting
statement: `lathe.config.json` MUST refuse a `checks` key as an unknown setting, naming it, since a product's checks are rows of its data.

title: A record with too many children of one kind is a warning
statement: A record with more children of one kind than the product's `max_children` setting MUST be a `too-many-children` warning that names the record, the kind and the count, and says to add a level between them, such as a capability or another aggregate. The children counted MUST be those of each kind of the five design stages, per kind: a test sits under the one record it proves and is read there, so it is not a child in a list.

title: The limit is the product's max_children setting, 15 by default
statement: The checks MUST read the limit from the product's `product_setting.max_children`, and use 15 when the product has no row. The store MUST refuse any value that is not a whole number of at least 1.

title: A capability with one child is a warning
statement: A capability with exactly one child MUST be a `lone-child` warning that names it and its child and says to merge it into a neighbor or give it more.

title: A lone child counts the record's own children of every kind
statement: The `lone-child` check MUST count every child of the capability, of any kind, and only its own children, not theirs. A capability with no children, or with two or more, MUST NOT be reported.

title: A flow's steps are counted per path
statement: `too-many-children` MUST count a flow's steps per path (a step with no path is on the main path), since each path reads as its own list, and its message MUST name the path when it is not main.

title: Grouped children are counted per group
statement: `too-many-children` MUST count the children of every kind with a `group_name` (UC requirements, view requirements, API requirements, pattern rules, standard rules and a product's own kinds alike) per `group_name`, read from the store's `record_group` view, the ungrouped ones as one list, with groups compared trimmed and in any letter case, since each group reads under its own heading; its message MUST name the group.

title: A group with one member is a lone child
statement: A group with exactly one member MUST get a `lone-child` warning on its parent, naming the group and its member, as a capability with one child does.

title: An aggregate with too many entities is a warning
statement: An aggregate with more entities than the product's `max_entities_per_aggregate` setting MUST be an `aggregate-too-large` warning that names the aggregate, its count and the limit, and says to split it into smaller aggregates that each change together.

title: The entities limit is the product's setting, 7 by default
statement: The check MUST read the limit from the product's `product_setting.max_entities_per_aggregate`, and use 7 when the product has no row. The store MUST refuse any value that is not a whole number of at least 1.

title: Each Product setting command changes one product's settings
statement: Each command of the Product setting aggregate (LA-CHK-A2) MUST load the product's settings it changes whole through ProductSettingRepository and write only the aggregate's own tables; a refused command MUST give every reason and change no file. The CLI (lathe product-setting <command>), the product_setting_ MCP tools and HTTP (POST /api/product-setting/<command>) MUST each name the one command they run.

title: Every problem of a product shows in one place, as the data is now
statement: Every problem the checks find in one product MUST be shown together, errors before warnings and grouped by check, with the problems that belong to no product, and MUST be shown as the data is after its latest change, without the Owner running a check.

title: A hand edit of a data file is refused and points at the tools
statement: The plugin's guard hook MUST refuse an Agent's Write, Edit, MultiEdit or NotebookEdit of a data file (a `.jsonl` file in the data folder `lathe.config.json` names) before it happens, saying to use Lathe's MCP tools or the `lathe` command instead.

title: Every other edit goes through silently
statement: The guard hook MUST let an edit of any other file through, with no output.

title: The plugin declares the guard hook and its scripts exist
statement: The plugin MUST declare the guard hook as a PreToolUse hook on Write, Edit, MultiEdit and NotebookEdit, and every script its hooks and MCP server name MUST exist.

title: The Reader finds a record in a domain
statement: The Reader MUST be able to open a domain, find a record in it by its ID or title, and open it.

title: The Reader follows a record's links
statement: From a record's page, the Reader MUST be able to follow any of its links, out or in, to the records at their ends, and back.

title: The Reader walks the model as a graph
statement: The Reader MUST be able to switch to the Graph stage of any page and move through the model by its boxes, from the mouse, the keyboard or touch.

title: The Reader walks the graph through the nav's groups
statement: In the graph, the Reader MUST reach every record through the same stages and kind groups the nav shows, each a place of its own.

title: The Reader reads a record as wiki, graph or model
statement: The Reader MUST be able to open any record at its one address and read it as a wiki page in the wiki card and as a graph, an ERD or a trace on the stage behind it, from the keyboard too.

title: The Reader reads a flow step by step
statement: The Reader MUST be able to read a flow's steps in order on each path, with what each invokes, where it happens and what it fulfills.

title: The Reader moves between products as spaces
statement: The Reader MUST be able to switch between products as spaces, each kept apart, and come back to where they were in each.

title: The rail shows only with two or more products
statement: The space rail MUST show only when the workspace shows two or more products. With one, the nav MUST show no rail and take its width, with the product's name and icon at the top of the nav; collapsed, the nav keeps its buttons and lists no spaces.

title: The Reader reads a product in its stage folders
statement: The Reader MUST find a product's records in the nav under Shared and each domain's five stages, as a real product's specs are laid out.

title: The Reader reads the technical specification and test plan by kind
statement: The Reader MUST find a domain's technical records and tests grouped by kind, in the nav, on the domain page and in the graph alike.

title: The Reader explores several places at once in tabs
statement: The Reader MUST be able to explore several places at once, each in a tab of its own with its own focus, stage, view and Back and Forward, open the same record in more than one, and find them all again after a reload.

title: The Reader reads a domain's ERD
statement: The Reader MUST be able to read a domain's model as an ERD of its aggregates, and each aggregate's own, in the ERD stage.

title: The Reader reads a record's history in the wiki card
statement: The Reader MUST be able to read a record's history, the commits that changed its rows and what each changed, in the wiki card without leaving the page.

title: The Reader reads a domain's endpoints and integrations
statement: The Reader MUST be able to find the endpoint that exposes a command or query, and the steps that exchange with an integration.

title: One definition of what changed
statement: What changed MUST be one record diff, the engine's (LA-EXP-QRY13), between the data now and a baseline, by record (its own row, the part rows it owns and the links it starts): each record added, removed, or changed field by field with each column before and after, its part rows added, removed or changed, and its links added and removed. Every place that shows a change (the stages' live marks, the Changes lens, the wiki card, the Changes panel and the desktop chat's per-turn diff) MUST use it and MUST NOT diff the data its own way.

title: Live marks on every stage as the data reloads
statement: Each time the data reloads, every stage (the Graph, the ERD and the Trace) MUST mark what the reload changed: an added record a soft glow and a "new" dot, a changed record a brief pulse in its own color then a lasting "changed" dot, a removed record a ghost outline that fades over a few seconds. Under reduced motion it MUST show the dots only, with no glow, pulse or fade.

title: The Changes lens dims everything unchanged since a baseline
statement: A Changes lens on every stage MUST dim every record unchanged since its baseline, with the stages' one fade and nothing laid out again. Its baseline picker MUST offer since the last commit (the default), since the branch left main (the merge base with the default branch) and since I last looked, which is kept per product per Reader in the session setting and moved to now when the Reader dismisses the lens or leaves the product.

title: The diff shows in the wiki card
statement: The wiki card of a record changed since the baseline MUST show what changed: each changed field old → new and the links added and removed. An added record's card MUST say "New since <baseline>".

title: Follow glides to each change as it lands
statement: Follow, off by default, MUST glide the camera to each change as it lands. Any camera move or focus by the Reader MUST turn it off, with a note saying so.

title: The Changes panel lists the changes
statement: A Changes panel over the stage MUST list the changes newest first, by record, each a card; clicking one MUST focus its record on the stage. Its toggle MUST show how many records changed.

title: loadWorkspace returns the Workspace contract
statement: `loadWorkspace(root)` MUST return a `Workspace` as defined in `lathe/src/types.ts`. Fields MAY be added to that contract but MUST NOT be renamed or removed.

title: Each record's product and domain come from its parents
statement: The engine MUST give each record its `product` and `domain` from its parent columns, through the store's `record_scope` table. Data the store refuses, such as a cycle of parents, MUST make the load end with one `data-refused` error per refusal, naming the file, line and rule, and no records, rather than loop or load in part.

title: Loading is fast enough to reload live
statement: `loadWorkspace(root)` MUST load Lathe's own spec in under 2 s, and load it again after one row changes in under 500 ms, on the dev machine, as `npm --prefix lathe run test:perf` measures, so the app and an agent's script can reload on every write. Every check still runs on every load. When the machine is busy (a one-minute load average above 12) the script measures but judges nothing, and a budget is never loosened. It MAY take `timings` in its options, which it fills with how long each phase took (open, files, checks, coverage, total).

title: Each load reads the data files afresh and writes nothing
statement: Each load MUST read the data files afresh, Lathe's own check rows beside the product's, into a new in-memory DuckDB through the store. The engine MUST NOT write the data to a database file or keep it between loads, so the data files stay the only source of truth; the one database file it keeps is the schema cache, which holds the migrated schema and never a product's data (LA-PLT-UC01-R11). It MAY keep the reference while no file in the data folders or the schema has changed.

title: A record with no owner belongs to the one domain that uses it
statement: The store's `record_scope` MUST give a view, an integration, a UI component and a value object the domain that uses it, worked out from the links and fields and never stored: a view the domains of the use cases whose flow steps happen in it; an integration those whose flow steps exchange with it; a UI component those that use the views it renders; a value object those of the entities, domain events and read models whose fields it types. When exactly one domain uses the record, that is its domain; when two or more do, or none, it has no domain and the product shares it. What sits under it (constraints, view requirements, their tests, a value type, an adapter, integration tests) MUST follow it. A specification keeps the domain its ID names. IDs stay product-scoped, so a record that gains or loses a using domain moves with no rename and no change to the data. Every check, coverage table and the app MUST read this one answer.

title: Each record is one row of its kind's table, one line of its file
statement: Each record MUST be one row of its kind's table, with typed columns, kept as one line of `data/<table>.jsonl`; its parts and its links MUST be rows of their own tables. The data files MUST be the source of truth: nothing else MAY hold a record's content, and the database built from them is never committed.

title: Line and column order do not change what a data file means
statement: Reordering the lines of a data file, or the columns of a line, MUST NOT change what the data means: a record's product, domain, parent and links come only from its columns, its ID and its relations' rows. A file in the data folder that is not a `.jsonl` file MUST be ignored.

title: An unknown parent is refused once
statement: A record whose parent column names no record MUST be refused once, as a foreign key naming the missing record and the kind it must be, and nothing else MAY be reported about that parent.

title: A link or parent the schema does not allow is refused once
statement: The store MUST refuse a link between two kinds its relation does not allow, naming the kinds that end accepts, and a parent column its kind does not have, each once.

title: A CLI command answers within a budget
statement: The engine MUST start fast enough that a cold CLI command, `lathe use-case get-use-case --id <id>` on Lathe's own spec run in a fresh process, finishes in under 800 ms on the dev machine, as `npm --prefix lathe run test:perf` measures, so an Agent can run one command per step, and the MCP server (which starts the same engine) answers its first call, without waiting on the engine's start-up; when the machine is busy (a one-minute load average above 12) the script measures but judges nothing, and the budget is never loosened.

title: The schema is cached, never the data, and a bad cache is never used
statement: The engine MUST start from a cached copy of the migrated schema (Lathe's, and a product's with its own kinds and relations) when there is one, and otherwise build it and cache it, one DuckDB file per schema in .cache/lathe of the node_modules folder that holds Lathe (or LATHE_CACHE_DIR), never in a product's files and never with a product's data; each file MUST be keyed by a hash of Lathe's and DuckDB's versions, the migrations, the engine's code and the product's declarations, and stamped with that key inside it, so a file whose stamp names another key, or that does not open, is never used and the schema is built afresh and cached again; a file MUST be written under a name of its own and renamed into place, so two processes that start at once never read half of one; and the cache MUST keep only the current base schema's files, and at most the 20 products' schemas written last.

title: An ID is used once
statement: An ID MUST be used by one record only, of any kind, in any product the store loads, so that an ID cited on its own (in a test name, a code file, the CLI or an app address) means exactly one record. A row that takes an ID in use MUST be refused once, as `unique-id`, naming the record that has it with its file and line, and the links to that ID MUST NOT be refused with it.

title: An ID fits its scope
statement: A record's ID MUST start with its parent's ID, its domain's ID or its product's ID and a hyphen, as its kind's ID scope says; a record with no owner starts with a product's ID, and a specification with a domain's.

title: Linked records share a product
statement: Every link, and every field typed by a value object or an aggregate, MUST join two records of the same product; an ID of another product in text is plain text, never a link.

title: An ID in text is kept as written and makes no link
statement: The engine MUST keep a record's text exactly as written, IDs, repeats, its own ID, code spans and fences included, and MUST NOT read a link, a mention or any other relation from it. Only a row of a relation's table relates two records.

title: No check reads text for IDs
statement: Checks MUST NOT report an ID in text, whether a record has it or not and whatever its prefix; the engine's one problem of its own is `data-refused`.

title: Init writes a config and a first product record
statement: `lathe init --name <name> --prefix <prefix>` MUST write `lathe.config.json` with this Lathe's schema version when the repo has none, and MUST add the product record with that ID and title to `data/product.jsonl` through the store. It MUST refuse a prefix that is not a valid ID and MUST NOT overwrite an existing product record.

title: The product's config names its data folder
statement: Every command MUST read the data folder from the `data` key of the product's `lathe.config.json`, defaulting to `data`, and MUST NOT read records from any other folder. A setting the config does not define MUST be refused with an error that names it.

title: A product adds its own kinds without forking Lathe
statement: A product's own kinds and relations MUST be `product_kind`, `product_kind_field` and `product_relation` rows in its own data, which add tables to the schema for that product only. They MUST NOT widen one of Lathe's kinds; that takes a migration.

title: Serve needs no build tools in the product repo
statement: `lathe serve` MUST serve the web app and its API for the product repo, and every other product its config lists, from the installed package alone, and open pages MUST reload when any of their data files change.

title: Each clone sets up the merge driver for the data files
statement: A product repo's `.gitattributes` MUST name its data files for the `lathe-data` merge driver (`**/data/*.jsonl merge=lathe-data`), and the README MUST say how each clone sets it up once with `git config merge.lathe-data.name` and `git config merge.lathe-data.driver "npx lathe merge-data %O %A %B %P"`, so two branches' new rows merge row by row instead of clashing line by line.

title: A stopped server leaves no database work running
statement: Stopping a server that `serve()` started MUST stop its watchers and take no more requests, MUST wait for any load, reload or write in progress and for the engine's background work, and MUST close its stores and, once no store in the process is open, the database engine before it resolves, so a process that exits then exits cleanly; `lathe serve` MUST stop this way on SIGINT and SIGTERM and then end by that signal.

title: The product's config names its test files
statement: The `tests` key of the product's `lathe.config.json` MUST list globs, relative to the product root, of the files that hold its test cases, defaulting to `**/*.test.{ts,tsx,js,mjs}` and `**/*.spec.{ts,tsx,js}`. Whatever the globs, files in node_modules, dist or a folder with its own `lathe.config.json` MUST NOT be read. A `tests` value that is not a non-empty list of globs MUST be refused, naming the key.

title: A workspace lists the other products it shows
statement: The `products` key of a workspace's `lathe.config.json` MUST list the folders, relative to its root, of the other products it shows, each holding its own `lathe.config.json` and data. Each MUST load beside the workspace's own product from its own folder, with its own config, schema version check, checks, tracing and coverage, as its own space. A listed folder that is the workspace itself, is listed twice or holds no `lathe.config.json`, a listed product that lists products of its own, and one product ID in two products' folders MUST be refused with an error that names it.

title: lathe check checks every product of the workspace
statement: `lathe check` at a workspace MUST check every product it shows, each in its own folder, and report each on its own (its errors, warnings and coverage, then its counts), then the counts of them all. It MUST exit 1 when any product has an error.

title: A folder with its own config is another product's, never the workspace's
statement: Tracing MUST treat a folder with its own `lathe.config.json` as another product's: the workspace's source files, test files, router files and default package folders MUST NOT include a file in it, and a package folder the workspace's config lists inside it MUST be refused, naming it.

title: Serve shows every product and writes to each one's own folder
statement: `lathe serve`, the app's dev server and the desktop app MUST serve every product the workspace shows, each as its own space, with each record's file and line in its own product's folder. A write MUST go to the data folder of the product whose records its commands name (a write that names none, such as a new product's, to the workspace's own), and a write that names records of two products MUST be refused with the reason.

title: Pages reload when any product's data files or Lathe's checks change
statement: When a file in the data folder of any product the workspace shows, or one of Lathe's own check rows or migrations, changes, the server SHOULD send `spec:changed`, and the open page SHOULD then load the data again without a manual refresh, staying at the same address.

title: A page reads again only what a change touched
statement: The server MUST announce each change (Data files changed) with the tables whose rows it changed and the read models whose projections read one of them, or every read model when the data loaded afresh or was refused; an open page MUST then read again only the reads of the read models named. After its own write, the page MUST wait for the server's change for that write, which the server sends before it answers, and read everything again only when no change comes within 300 ms or no channel is open.

title: A change reloads only the tables it changed
statement: When data files change, the store MUST read again only the changed files' tables, a change set from one write or a burst of writes being one reload, and hold them at once to the keys (each row's foreign keys, every row pointing into them, their unique keys, every ID once across kinds) and to the rules of each aggregate whose rules read a changed table; it MUST build again only the read models whose projections read a changed table. The rest of the whole build (the database's checks, the integrity queries and every aggregate's rules) MUST then run in the background, and data it refuses MUST be refused. A reload and a load from scratch of the same files MUST give the same rows on the same lines, the same refusal, the same reads and the same problems, coverage and chains. A changed declaration of the product's own kinds or relations, or a file of no table, MUST load every file afresh.

title: The checks run in the background after a burst of changes
statement: After a change to the data, by a command or by anything else, the server MUST run the check rows and coverage in the background on the data built whole, 150 ms after the last change and the last request on the data have answered, so that a burst of changes (a git pull, an Agent's writes) makes one run and the reads a change sets off (a page reading again what changed) answer before the run holds the server, though never more than 1 s after the change; it MUST answer the problems and coverage from the last run meanwhile, and MUST announce the checks' read models when the run is ready. A command still refuses on its aggregate's rules before saving, and its commit MUST refuse whatever the data's whole build would refuse: it holds the new state to the keys and the rules of each aggregate that reads a changed table, then, over the data last built whole with the tables that differ beside it, to those rows' column constraints and every integrity query, building the data whole only when the command changes the product's kinds or relations or something is refused, so that the whole build follows in the background as after a reload.

title: A large product stays within its budgets
statement: On the large product (LA-PLT-TD04, about ten times Lathe's records), served as `lathe serve` serves it on the dev machine, one edit to a data file MUST be visible in under 500 ms from the file's change (the reload, the rules it reruns and the reads the change names, read again), and so MUST one of the page's own writes from its request (the command's commit and the same reads); the checks' run after it MUST be announced within 4 s of the change; and a cold load with every check MUST take under 4 s, as `npm --prefix lathe run test:perf` measures. The budgets are never loosened to make a run pass.

title: The Reader works the whole app from the keyboard
statement: The Reader MUST be able to reach and run every command of the app from the keyboard, by its VS Code key or from the palette, and hear what it changed.

title: The Reader learns a shortcut where it is used
statement: Wherever a command can be run, the Reader MUST be able to learn its keys there: in its tooltip, the palette, the shortcuts sheet and to a screen reader, all from one keymap.

title: The Reader arranges the workbench and it stays so
statement: The Reader MUST be able to resize, hide and bring back the panels of the workbench, by pointer or keyboard, and find them as they left them.

title: The Reader chooses or makes a theme for the whole app
statement: The Reader MUST be able to choose a theme and a color mode that apply to the whole app at once, make, share and import a theme of their own, and choose whether scroll zooms the stages or pans them.

title: The Reader reads and moves around Lathe on a phone
statement: On a phone, the Reader MUST be able to find a record, read it, switch its view and move between pages, with text they can read and targets sized for a finger.

title: Nothing the Reader is looking at jumps
statement: As the Reader opens pages, moves around, resizes and reloads, nothing they are looking at MUST move unless they moved it.

title: Big maps stay smooth
statement: On a product of about ten times Lathe's records, the Graph, the ERD and the Trace MUST pan and zoom with no frame over 20 ms (60 frames a second), the arrow walk MUST frame a new focus within 200 ms, and each map MUST be laid out off the main thread (the Graph's within 4 s) and again only when what it reads changes, the map before it staying on screen and answering the camera, so panning keeps 60 frames a second through a reload, as the performance suite measures (`app/perf/big-maps.perf.ts`, budgets in `app/perf/budgets.ts`).

title: The Reader uses Lathe by keyboard and screen reader
statement: Every page and control MUST be usable by keyboard and screen reader, at WCAG 2.2 AA.

title: Open Product Folder picks a folder and opens it in its own window
statement: File › Open Product Folder… (Cmd+O, Ctrl+O elsewhere) MUST let the reader choose a folder and open it in a window of its own. A folder that is not a product MUST be refused with a message saying what is missing.

title: The window names the product and its folder
statement: The window's title MUST be the names of the products in the folder (the titles of their product records, joined by commas), then the folder, with the home folder shown as `~`. The page MUST NOT change it.

title: A window opens with the shell background, with no white flash
statement: A window MUST stay hidden until its page is ready to show, and its background MUST be the app's shell color (`--shell`) for the system's light or dark appearance, so it never flashes white.

title: The page reaches the shell only through window.latheDesktop
statement: Every window MUST run its page with context isolation and the sandbox on and Node integration off. The preload MUST expose only `window.latheDesktop` with `isDesktop`, `platform`, `onCommand` and `setChrome`, and nothing of Node or Electron.

title: Links that leave the app open in the system browser
statement: A link to any other origin than the window's own server MUST open in the system browser, and the window MUST NOT navigate away from Lathe or open windows of its own.

title: Quitting waits for every window's server to stop
statement: When the app quits, also when it is stopped from a terminal, it MUST wait until the server of every window, closed ones included, has stopped before the process exits, so it always exits cleanly even while a reload is in progress, and MUST give up waiting after 10 seconds so a server that hangs cannot keep it from quitting.

title: A workspace opens with every product it lists
statement: Opening a workspace's folder MUST show every product its `lathe.config.json` lists, beside its own, in the one window; the title MUST name them all, and a record's data file MUST be found in its own product's data folder.

title: The desktop app opens a product with its own installed Lathe
statement: The desktop app MUST serve a product with the product's own built Lathe (`node_modules/@jaredrob/lathe`) when it has one, and with its bundled copy otherwise, and its About window MUST say which, with the version, for the product in front.

title: The app remembers the recent folders and each window's place
statement: File › Open Recent MUST list the folders opened last and reopen one, and MUST be able to clear the list; the next launch MUST reopen the last folder; and a window MUST keep its size and place when it moves, resizes or closes, and reopen there.

title: Development loads the 5199 dev server when it serves the opened folder
statement: In development a window MUST load `http://localhost:5199` when that server answers for the opened folder, so app changes hot-reload exactly as in the browser.

title: Otherwise the shell starts a dev server of its own for the folder
statement: When 5199 does not answer, or answers for another folder, the shell MUST start the app's Vite dev server on a free port with `LATHE_ROOT` set to the opened folder, and load it. The dev API plugin MUST read its product folder from `LATHE_ROOT`, defaulting to Lathe's own repo, so the owner's 5199 server is unchanged.

title: A change to the main process or preload restarts Electron
statement: `npm --prefix desktop run dev` MUST rebuild the shell and restart Electron whenever a file under `desktop/src` changes. A build that fails MUST leave the running shell as it is.

title: Record changes reload the page in every mode
statement: A change to the opened product's specs MUST reload what the page shows, whether it loads `serve()`, the shell's own dev server or the 5199 server.

title: A local build is unsigned and stays on this Mac
statement: `npm --prefix desktop run pack` MUST build Lathe first, then an unsigned macOS app for this Mac's architecture in `desktop/release/`, which git ignores. It MUST NOT sign, notarize, publish or add auto-update.

title: The app can tell it runs in the desktop app
statement: `window.latheDesktop.isDesktop` MUST be true in the desktop app and absent in a browser, so the keymap can show desktop-only bindings later.

title: A menu choice runs the same command as its key
statement: The menu bar MUST have File, Edit, View, Window and Help, and choosing an item that stands for one of the app's commands MUST run that command by its ID in the page, as its key would.

title: The Reader works under Lathe's own title bar
statement: In the desktop app, the Reader MUST be able to go back and forward, open quick find, toggle the panels and move the window from Lathe's own title bar, which follows the theme.

title: A second launch or a folder from Finder goes to the running app
statement: The app MUST run as one instance: a second launch, or a folder opened through Finder or the Dock, MUST open that folder's window in the running app, or bring it forward when it is open.

title: The window behaves like a native one
statement: The window MUST NOT check spelling, MUST use overlay scroll bars and native context menus (Cut, Copy and Paste on text), and MUST reopen in full screen when it was closed in full screen. In full screen on macOS the title bar MUST drop the room it keeps for the hidden traffic lights.

title: macOS keeps no window state for Lathe
statement: The app MUST opt out of macOS window restoration (`ApplePersistenceIgnoreState`, `NSQuitAlwaysKeepsWindows`), since it reopens its own windows, so a run that was killed leaves macOS nothing to offer to reopen.

title: Lathe sits in the Dock and the app menu as a Mac app does
statement: Lathe's Dock icon MUST read at every size, its Dock badge MUST count the check errors the window in front reports, and its Dock menu MUST open another folder and list the recent ones; About Lathe MUST show the versions that run and Settings… MUST open Appearance; and a folder the engine cannot load MUST open an error page that says why, with a way on.

title: The app writes through each command's own route
statement: The app MUST change data only by sending one command's fields to that command's route, `POST /api/<aggregate>/<command>`, which MUST run it in its own transaction and answer with the rows it changed, or with 422 and the refusal's every reason.

title: Only the app's own pages can write
statement: The server MUST refuse a command that comes from another site's page, that is not JSON, or whose body is over 1 MB, before the command runs.

title: Lathe loads only data for its own schema version
statement: Every load (the CLI, the server, the MCP tools, `loadWorkspace` and `openStore`) MUST stop, reading no data, when `lathe.config.json` names another schema version than Lathe's, with one message: for an older one "This product's data is for schema N; this Lathe uses schema M. Run `npx lathe upgrade` to move it forward.", for a newer one that it needs a newer Lathe: update @jaredrob/lathe. A config with no schema version MUST be read as version 1, and one that is not a whole number from 1 MUST be refused.

title: Upgrade converts the data in order and loads it
statement: `lathe upgrade` MUST run the converters in `lathe/upgrades/` in order from the product's schema version to Lathe's, each on the raw rows of the data files. Only once the converted data loads under the new schema, with every aggregate's rules, MUST it raise the config's schema version, and print what each converter changed. It MUST refuse when a converter is missing, and MUST NOT keep or read the old form afterwards.

title: Upgrade lists what it could not convert
statement: What a converter cannot convert MUST be printed as a to-do list for the Owner, never dropped. When the converted data does not load, the upgrade MUST stop without raising the schema version and list the store's refusals as the to-dos.

title: Upgrade refuses a working tree with changes
statement: `lathe upgrade` MUST refuse, changing nothing, when the product's git working tree has changes or the product is not under git, so the upgrade is one reviewable commit.

title: The plugin warns once when its skills are for another major version
statement: The plugin's MCP launcher MUST read the product's installed Lathe version and schema version, and when the installed major version is not the one the plugin's manifest says its skills were written for (`lathe.major`), MUST add one warning naming both to the first tool result, and to no other.

title: Outside a Lathe repo the launcher says why it cannot start
statement: When the folder Claude Code runs in holds no Lathe repo, the plugin's MCP launcher MUST say why it cannot start, and start nothing.

title: A command takes its fields as JSON from any interface
statement: Every command MUST take its fields as one JSON object in its MCP tool's shape: the MCP tool as its arguments, HTTP as its body and the CLI with `--json -` (stdin) or `--json <file>`, read by one reader, with text kept exactly as given and the same validation and refusals as its flags; the CLI MUST refuse `--json` given with field flags as bad usage, and print the result as JSON.

title: The plugin's skills write only through the tools
statement: The plugin's skills MUST tell the Agent to change data only through the aggregates' MCP tools or CLI commands, never by editing data files. Every tool they name MUST be one of an aggregate's own commands or queries, and every example in them MUST run such a tool with the fields it takes, with values of their types.

title: The Owner talks with their own Claude Code
statement: In the desktop app, the Owner MUST be able to talk with their own Claude Code, run in the product folder with their login and settings, in a chat panel beside the stage, and never through an API key or an agent loop of Lathe's own.

title: Claude's answers link the records they name
statement: Claude's answers MUST read as rich text, and a record ID in them MUST open that record on the stage.

title: Claude's work shows as tool rows and record diffs
statement: Each tool call Claude makes MUST show as a compact row that expands to its input and result, and the records the spec gained, lost or changed during a turn MUST show by record, from the one record diff (LA-EXP-QRY13) of the spec before the turn against the spec after it.

title: The Owner answers permission prompts and stops a turn
statement: A tool call that needs the Owner's permission MUST wait for their answer in the chat (allow once or deny), and the Owner MUST be able to stop the turn under way.

title: The Owner resumes, forks or starts a session
statement: The Owner MUST be able to resume or fork any of the folder's saved Claude Code sessions, listed by title and date, or start a new one, and MUST be warned, with a fork offered, when the session may be open in another Claude client.

title: Claude sees the Reader's focus and opens records
statement: Claude MUST be able to ask what the Reader is looking at (the focused record, the stage and the selection) and to open a record in the window, and both MUST refuse when no app window is connected.

title: Claude reaches the window from a shell too
statement: The CLI MUST offer what the app tools do, `lathe app focus` and `lathe app open <id> [--stage graph|erd|trace]`, through the same bridge and the same code, refusing with exit 1 when no app window is connected.

title: Every chat brings Lathe's own tools
statement: Every chat session the desktop app starts MUST load the Lathe plugin of the Lathe the window runs (the product's own installed Lathe's, else the app's own), its tools running that same Lathe whatever the Owner has installed, and MUST list each Lathe tool once when the Owner has the plugin installed too.

title: The Owner chooses what Claude may do without asking
statement: The Owner MUST be able to choose the chat's permission mode in one control: Ask (every tool asks, reads included), Accept reads (the default: reads run without asking, everything else asks), Auto (Claude Code's auto mode decides), Bypass (nothing asks; turned on only after a warning, and marked while on) or View only (only reads: every Lathe command, and every tool that writes files or runs code, is withheld or refused, the refusal saying the chat is View only). A new chat MUST start in the mode the folder's last chat had.

title: The chat says what it runs with
statement: The chat MUST show how many Lathe tools the session has and from which Lathe, and when `claude` is not found or not signed in MUST say so with the fix (where to install it, or `/login`) before the first message, instead of failing on it.

title: A tool can be allowed for the rest of the chat
statement: A permission prompt MUST offer to allow its tool always in this chat, after which that tool MUST run without asking for the rest of the chat; View only's refusals still hold.

title: Claude knows where the Owner is
statement: Each message MUST carry, as context apart from the Owner's own words, what they are looking at in the window (the product, the page, the stage, the focused record and the selection), shown as a chip above the message box that they can remove; Claude MUST be told to start from it, and to use app_focus and app_open, never a search of the code, for anything else about the window.

title: The Owner dictates a message, recognized on the Mac
statement: Where the Mac can recognize speech on-device, the Owner MUST be able to dictate a message from the mic button or its rebindable key, its words appearing in the message box as they speak, to edit before sending; the audio MUST NOT leave the Mac nor be recorded or saved, the Owner MUST be told so before macOS first asks for the microphone, and where on-device recognition is not available the mic MUST be hidden.

title: Voice activation wakes the chat, and commands act on the draft
statement: With voice activation on, "Lathe" (or the wake phrase chosen) said after a pause MUST open the message box and start dictating, the rest of the utterance becoming the message, and MUST NOT wake the chat mid-sentence; while dictating, a pause, the wake phrase and a command word ending the utterance MUST send, clear, remove the last sentence or start a paragraph, and any other words MUST stay text; about 20 seconds of quiet MUST end dictation and leave the draft.

title: The chat listens only in front, and only when asked
statement: Voice activation MUST be off until the Owner turns it on, and the chat MUST listen only while its window is in front: going behind another window or app stops listening and leaves the draft.

title: Quick mode sends when the Owner has finished
statement: With Quick mode on, a dictated message MUST be sent by itself after a pause judged on the Mac from the words and the voice's pitch: about half a second after a finished thought, 3 to 4 seconds mid-thought and about 2 seconds when unsure, or a fixed 2 seconds where the voice cannot be read; a countdown MUST show on Send, and any sound or key MUST cancel it.

title: Coverage counts designed and proved obligations
statement: For each domain, coverage MUST give the number of obligations of each obligation kind, and how many of each are designed and how many are proved. Built counts are LA-TRC-UC01-R04; not-automated-yet counts are LA-TRC-UC02-R03.

title: Coverage lists each gap with what it lacks
statement: Coverage MUST list each obligation that is not designed, not built or not proved, with its kind, saying which it lacks, and the `not-designed`, `not-built` and `not-proved` warnings MUST name exactly the obligations coverage counts as lacking it.

title: Coverage gaps are warnings, not errors
statement: A gap MUST be reported as a warning, so that an honest, unfinished design still passes `lathe check`.

title: Coverage reports built separately from designed
statement: For each domain, coverage MUST give how many obligations of each kind are built: every technical record that implements its design names a file that exists, and there is at least one. The built count MUST never be more than the designed count, so a domain whose code does not exist yet shows as designed but not built.

title: Coverage lists each record short of a minimum as a gap named by its rule
